title: Dopamine Menu: How to Design Your Own Reward System

shots.voiceover: What if your brain had a menu of things guaranteed to work when you're stuck? You can build that.
shots.textOverlay: the dopamine menu -- ADHD productivity hack

shots.voiceover: You're stuck. Can't start. Brain is flat. Scrolling. The usual. What do you reach for? Social media — works for 3 minutes. Food — same. TV — pulls you under for 2 hours. None of these are actually recharging you. They're borrowing dopamine from tomorrow.

ADHD researcher and author Ned Hallowell coined the dopamine menu concept: a pre-curated list of activities that give your brain a genuine dopamine hit without the cortisol crash afterward. The key distinction is activities that energize versus activities that numb. Energizing: brief physical movement, a 5-minute creative task, a song you love, a glass of water and a change of room. Numbing: doomscrolling, food, passive TV. Both feel good immediately — only one leaves you ready to start work.
shots.textOverlay: energize vs. numb -- only one leaves you ready

shots.voiceover: Your dopamine menu is personal. Write down 5 things that take under 5 minutes, feel genuinely good, and don't spiral. That's your stuck-brain emergency kit. When BoxDay detects you haven't logged a task in a while, we nudge you toward yours.
